claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes multistep crystallization during reheating.
A short isothermal hold in the supercooled-liquid region after rapid cooling will increase amorphous retention relative to continuous cooling and reheating.
The isothermal hold will increase the alloy's thermal stability.
The hold temperature must lie strictly between Tg and Tx.
The initial cooling rate must be high enough to bypass significant crystallization.
The isothermal hold reduces nucleation activity of the primary non-eutectic phases.
The isothermal hold stabilizes short-range atomic order without permitting long-range crystallization.
The hold facilitates atomic rearrangements that favor formation and stabilization of the amorphous state.
The hold hinders extensive nucleation of primary crystallites.
Locking in the supercooled-liquid structure during the hold minimizes the driving force for crystallization.
The proposed mechanism raises the effective crystallization-onset temperature during subsequent reheating.
Samples receiving the hold will show an upward shift in DSC crystallization-onset temperature relative to samples without the hold.
Standard rapid or slow cooling followed by continuous reheating typically produces extensive primary crystallization.
The baseline protocol produces lower apparent thermal stability in DSC than the proposed hold protocol.
A decreased DSC crystallization-exotherm intensity or area indicates improved amorphous retention.

contradictions.description: The intervention places the hold immediately after rapid cooling at a temperature between Tg and Tx, but the conditions first cool the sample below Tg and then call for a hold between Tg and Tx without specifying the required reheating step.
